title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The Screen Flow map stops guessing
summary: A navigation whose destination is a variable no longer draws an arrow to an arbitrary screen, and the legend counts what is actually on screen.

highlights.title: No arrow without evidence
highlights.description: A `navigate(dest)` the parser cannot resolve used to match the first declared route with the same number of segments. On a graph with a profile screen and an orders screen, both taking one argument, the arrow was a coin flip. It now draws nothing.

highlights.title: Interpolated routes keep what they know
highlights.description: `navigate("${Screen.Profile.route}/$userId")` is resolved against the route constants of the workspace before the placeholders are applied, so a target the parser could pin exactly is no longer thrown away.

highlights.title: The legend matches the drawing
highlights.description: Navigations from outside any composable, and targets no screen declares, have no box to start or end at. They were counted in the header and never drawn.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Two declared routes matching the same target no longer let the map pick one. It keeps the literal target, which is either a real screen or nothing.
A route constant declared with the same name and two different values in two modules resolves to nothing, instead of taking the value of whichever file was read last.
An arrow no longer changes destination after a file rename, since it no longer depends on the order the workspace is scanned in.
